facts.fact: The context menu of a Job in the tree view has the entry 'Update Tools from Library'. The icon is CAM_UpdateDocumentTools.svg. The entry examines only that Job.

When the Job has no tool that is different from the library, 'Update Tools from Library' shows an information box with the title 'Update Tools from Library' and the text 'This job has no tool updates available.'

When a document becomes active for the first time after it is opened, FreeCAD examines all Jobs of the document and shows the dialog only when a minimum of one tool is different from the library. The check occurs one time for each load of a document, after restore and recompute are complete.

The check at document load occurs only when the preference 'Check for tool updates from the library when opening a document' is set. The Job context-menu entry operates always, with the preference set or not set.

The Assets page of the CAM preferences has the checkbox 'Check for tool updates from the library when opening a document'. The parameter is the boolean `ToolUpdateOnLoad` in `BaseApp/Preferences/Mod/CAM/Tools`. The default is True (set). The checkbox is below the Machines group and is not in a group box.

The dialog title is 'Tool Updates Available'. The text at the top is: "'{}' has tools that differ from the library (newer presets, changed dimensions - e.g. a regrind - or both). Updating replaces the whole tool with the current library version and recomputes the document - expand a row to review before applying." The name in the text is the document label at document load and the Job label from the context menu.

The dialog table has one row for each stale tool and five columns: a checkbox column without a header text, 'Job', 'Tool #', 'Tool' and 'Changes'. The rows are in the sequence of the Job label and then the tool number. 'Tool #' shows the Tool Number of the Tool Controller and 'Tool' shows the label of the embedded Tool Bit.
Each row has a checkbox that is set by default. A checkbox in the table header with the tooltip 'Select all' sets or clears all rows and shows a partial state when only some rows are set.
The dialog buttons are 'Update' and 'Cancel'. 'Cancel' is the default button. 'Update' is disabled when no row is set. 'Update' replaces only the tools of the set rows. 'Cancel' changes nothing.

The 'Changes' cell shows the summary 'Presets', 'Geometry' or 'Presets, Geometry'. Only when a tool has geometry changes, the cell is a tree that the reader can expand. The tree then shows one line 'Presets' if the presets are different, and one line for each changed property in the form '<property label>: <old value> → <new value>'. The presets are not shown item by item.
The old value and the new value in the Changes tree are shown in the `Units` of the library Tool Bit (Metric or Imperial), not in the units of the embedded Tool Bit.

FreeCAD finds the library Tool Bit of an embedded Tool Bit only by the `ToolBitID` property. An embedded Tool Bit without a `ToolBitID`, or with a `ToolBitID` that is not in the local library store, is not in the dialog and is not changed.

An embedded Tool Bit is stale when its Feeds & Speeds presets (the `Presets` property) are different from the library Tool Bit, or when a property of the property group 'Shape' that is on the two Tool Bits has a different value. A tool that has no difference is not in the dialog.
FreeCAD does not compare the geometry when the `ShapeType` of the embedded Tool Bit and of the library Tool Bit are different. A property that is on only one of the two Tool Bits is not compared.

An update always replaces the full Tool Bit: FreeCAD attaches a new full copy of the library Tool Bit to the document, sets the `Tool` property of the Tool Controller to the new copy, and removes the old Tool Bit object from the document. A partial update (only presets or only geometry) is not possible.

facts.fact: Because the update removes the old Tool Bit object, all local edits of the embedded Tool Bit (presets, dimensions and other properties) are lost for each tool that is updated. The new copy also has the `Units` of the library Tool Bit.
After the update, FreeCAD hides the new Tool Bit in the 3D view if it is visible, and recomputes the document one time if a minimum of one tool was replaced.
A tool whose library Tool Bit was deleted between the check and the click on 'Update' is not replaced and stays as it is.
The Feeds & Speeds presets that are edited on an embedded Tool Bit are written only to the `Presets` property of the document object. They are not written to the library.

A Tool Bit has the property `Units` (type App::PropertyEnumeration, group 'Attributes', description 'Measurement units for the tool bit'). The values are 'Metric' and 'Imperial'. The default is 'Metric'.

FreeCAD saves each quantity parameter of a Tool Bit in the `Units` of the Tool Bit, with 3 decimals for Metric and 4 decimals for Imperial. The active unit schema and the Units Decimals preference do not change the saved text when `Units` is 'Metric' or 'Imperial'.

facts.fact: A metric value that FreeCAD shows in µm (a small value) is saved with 4 decimals, not 3. An angle is saved with the degree symbol directly after the number, without a space.

When a Tool Bit has no usable `Units` value, FreeCAD uses the active unit schema to select the unit and the number of decimals: 4 decimals when the active schema is the Imperial schema (schema 3), 3 decimals for all other schemas.

When the ToolBit editor loads a Tool Bit whose `Units` is 'Metric' or 'Imperial', the editor sets the unit schema of FreeCAD to that value (Metric = schema 6, Imperial = schema 3). The editor sets the initial schema again when it closes. A change of `Units` in the editor builds the property fields again in the new units.
The quantity fields of the ToolBit editor show 3 decimals in Metric and 4 decimals in Imperial. The Units Decimals preference does not change the number of decimals in these fields.
Each Tool Bit file that FreeCAD supplies in Tools/Bit (15 `.fctb` files) has the parameter "Units" in the "parameter" object, for example "Units": "Metric".

A double-click on a Tool Bit in the tree view of a document opens the ToolBit editor as a task panel. OK saves the Tool Bit and recomputes the document. Cancel aborts the transaction 'Edit ToolBit', thus all edits of the panel are discarded.

facts.fact: The Transform entry of the tree-view context menu on a Tool Bit in a document starts the standard Transform manipulator (command Std_TransformManip). It does not open the ToolBit editor. The context menu of a Tool Bit has no CAM entry of its own.

The command CAM_ToolBitDock has the menu text 'Add Toolbit…', the tooltip 'Opens the toolbit selection dialog' and the shortcut P, T. It opens a dialog with the title 'Toolbit Selector'. The buttons are 'Open Library Editor', 'Add to Job' and 'Close'.

The library drop-down of the Toolbit Selector always has the entry 'All Tools' as the first entry, before the libraries. The libraries follow in natural sort sequence of their labels. 'All Tools' shows all Tool Bits of the asset store, in a library or not.
A Tool Bit that is selected in 'All Tools' has no library tool number. A Tool Bit that is selected in a library has the tool number of that library as the suggested number.

A double-click on a Tool Bit, or 'Add to Job' with one or more selected Tool Bits, adds one Tool Controller for each Tool Bit. 'Add to Job' is enabled only when a Tool Bit is selected and the document has a Job. The new Tool Controller has the label 'TC: <Tool Bit label>'.

When the Toolbit Selector is opened by the 'Add Toolbit…' command or by the Tool Controller drop-down of an Operation, and the Tool Bit has no library tool number, an input dialog with the title 'Tool Number' and the label 'Tool number for {}:' (the Tool Bit label) asks for the number. The default is the next free number of the Job and the minimum is 1.

When the library tool number of the Tool Bit is already used in the Job by a different tool, the 'Tool Number' input dialog always opens, with the label 'Tool number {} is already used by {}.' and, on the next line, 'Tool number for {}:'. The values are the used number, the label of the Tool Controller that has it, and the Tool Bit label. The default is the next free number of the Job.

The 'Tool Number' input dialog opens again as long as the number that the reader gives is used by a different tool. Cancel in this dialog does not add that Tool Bit; the other selected Tool Bits are still added.
The next free number of a Job is the highest Tool Number of the Tool Controllers in the Job plus 1. It is 1 when the Job has no Tool Controller. A lower number that is not used is not selected.
When the library tool number is free in the Job, or the same tool already uses it, FreeCAD gives that number to the new Tool Controller and does not ask.

When the document has no Job, 'Add to Job' shows a message with the title 'No Job Found' and the text 'Create a Job first.' When the document has more than one Job and no Job was given to the dialog, FreeCAD asks which Job gets the Tool Controllers.

Two Tool Controllers have a tool number conflict only when they have the same `ToolNumber` and their Tool Bits have different `ToolBitID` values. Tool Controllers whose Tool Bits have the same `ToolBitID` can have the same Tool Number; this is how one tool gets more than one set of feeds and speeds.

When the reader changes the tool number in the Tool Controller editor to a number that a different tool in the Job uses, FreeCAD does not change `ToolNumber`, sets the field back to the old number and shows a warning with the title 'Tool Number In Use' and the text 'Tool number {} is already used by {}.' (the number and the label of the Tool Controller that has it).

The command CAM_ToolController ('Tool Controller', tooltip 'Adds a new tool controller to the active job') is not in a menu or a toolbar. It stays registered for macros and opens the Toolbit Selector for the selected Job with the request for a tool number.
An update from the library sets the `Tool` property of the Tool Controller to the new library copy. The update code changes no other property of the Tool Controller.
The GUI page of the CAM preferences (window title 'GUI') has the group box 'Tool Bit Shape Drawing' with four controls. All four parameters are in `BaseApp/Preferences/Mod/CAM`.
'Dimension color (light theme)': color button, parameter `ToolBitDimensionColorLight`, default #111111 (RGB 17, 17, 17), tooltip 'Color of the dimension lines and labels on a light theme'.
'Dimension color (dark theme)': color button, parameter `ToolBitDimensionColorDark`, default #23818d (RGB 35, 129, 141), tooltip 'Color of the dimension lines and labels on a dark theme'.
'Dimension highlight color': color button, parameter `ToolBitDimensionHighlightColor`, default #ff8c00 (RGB 255, 140, 0), tooltip 'Color of the dimension the mouse is pointing at'.

'Tool artwork brightness (dark theme)': spin box with the suffix ' %', parameter `ToolBitArtworkBrightness` (integer), default 85, minimum 10, maximum 100. The tooltip is 'How brightly the tool itself is drawn on a dark theme. The artwork is drawn for a white page, so it is dimmed to keep it from glaring.' The code also limits a stored value to the range 10 to 100.
For the Chamfer Tool Shape, FreeCAD calculates `Diameter` as TipDiameter + 2 × CuttingEdgeHeight × tan(CuttingEdgeAngle / 2). `Diameter` is not an input.

The ToolBit editor does not show a calculated parameter, thus the Chamfer editor form has no `Diameter` field. The property view shows the Chamfer `Diameter` as read-only. FreeCAD calculates the value again when the Tool Bit properties are updated.

The Chamfer Tool Shape has these parameters and labels: `CuttingEdgeAngle` 'Cutting edge angle', `CuttingEdgeHeight` 'Cutting edge height', `Diameter` 'Diameter', `Flutes` 'Flutes', `Length` 'Overall tool length', `ShankDiameter` 'Shank diameter', `TipDiameter` 'Tip diameter'. Only the Chamfer shape was changed to have a calculated parameter in this unit.

The preset dialog (window title 'Edit preset') has the group box 'Notes' with a text field for more than one line. The text is saved in the key "notes" of the preset record. Empty notes are saved as null.
The table of the Presets tab has the columns 'Name', 'Material', 'Op type', 'Surface speed', 'Chipload' and 'Notes'. The 'Notes' cell shows the notes on one line and the tooltip shows the full text.
The buttons of the Presets tab are 'Add preset', 'Edit', 'Copy' and 'Delete', in this sequence. A double-click on a table row opens the preset for edit.

A preset must have a name. When the 'Name:' field is empty or has only spaces, OK shows a warning with the title 'Name required' and the text 'Give the preset a name.' and the dialog stays open. The placeholder text of the field is "e.g. 'Aluminum aggressive'".

The identity of a preset is the name together with the material and the op type. Two presets of one Tool Bit can have the same name only if the material or the op type is different. If all three are the same, OK shows a warning with the title 'Duplicate preset' and the text "This tool already has a preset named '%s' for this material and op type." and the dialog stays open.

'Copy' operates only when a preset is selected. It opens the preset dialog with the values of the selected preset and with the name selected for edit. On OK, FreeCAD adds a new preset; the selected preset does not change. The name rule also applies, thus the reader must change the name, the material or the op type.

The Camotics export writes, for each tool, the keys "units", "shape", "length", "diameter" and "description". "units" is "imperial" when the active unit schema shows the tool diameter in an imperial unit (in, ", thou, ft, '), and "metric" in all other conditions.

The Camotics export writes "diameter" and "length" as numbers in inches when "units" is "imperial" and in millimeters when "units" is "metric". The unit of the diameter decides the unit for the two values of a tool. The `Units` property of the Tool Bit is not used.

The Camotics export rounds "diameter" and "length" to the number of decimals of the Units Decimals preference (integer parameter `Decimals` in `BaseApp/Preferences/Units`; the code uses 2 when the parameter is not set).

The Camotics import reads the "units" key of each tool: "imperial" gives `Diameter` and `Length` in inches, "metric" gives millimeters. When the key is absent or has a different value, the import uses millimeters.

The Camotics shape names are: ballend and taperedballnose to "Ballnose", endmill to "Cylindrical", v-bit and vbit to "Conical", chamfer to "Snubnose". All other Tool Shapes are exported as "Cylindrical". The serializer label is 'Camotics Tool Library' and the file extension is .json.

The file CAM_UpdateDocumentTools.svg is in src/Mod/CAM/Gui/Resources/icons/ and is registered in Path.qrc. It is the icon of the 'Update Tools from Library' context-menu entry and of the 'Tool Updates Available' dialog (window icon and 64 × 64 image at the top).
